sentences.text: Quetecsaurus means "fire lizard" and is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur.
The humerus of Quetecsaurus has a unique shape featuring a strongly S-shaped proximal border, a rounded proximomedial border, and an angular proximolateral corner.
Quetecsaurus was first described and named by Bernardo González Riga and Leonardo Ortiz David in 2014.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was collected from mudstones of the Cerro Lisandro Formation in the Neuquén Basin.
This specimen represents the first sauropod with well-preserved materials recovered from the Cerro Lisandro Formation.
Quetecsaurus is classified within Titanosauria and is considered most closely related to Mendozasaurus and Futalognkosaurus, which are members of Lognkosauria.
Preliminary phylogenetic analysis places Quetecsaurus as a sister taxon to the clade formed by Mendozasaurus and Futalognkosaurus.
Quetecsaurus is related to Mendozasaurus and Futalognkosaurus based on the presence of three lateral laminae on its neural spines.
Quetecsaurus fossils are known from the Late Cretaceous of the southern Mendoza Province in western Argentina.
Quetecsaurus lived during the Turonian stage of the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 93 to 89 million years ago.
The time range for Quetecsaurus is the Turonian stage, from 93.9 to 89.8 million years ago.
